compare.intro: This unit's points come in look-alike sets: くせに blames a person, のに tells a fact with surprise or disappointment, and ながら（も） is a calmer, more formal although that joins the ます stem, an い-adjective or a noun directly; ても〜ても says trying again and again changes nothing, while たとえ〜ても imagines one case that may never happen; といっても makes what you just said sound smaller, while にしても accepts something and then gives your own judgement; [反面|はんめん] shows two sides of one thing, 一方で can also set two different things side by side, and けれども is the everyday but that can also lead into a request; わりに measures a result against a degree such as size, price or effort (a noun takes の), while にしては judges one case against what you would expect of it and joins a noun directly.

forms.tag: 程度とのずれ · for (a degree or amount)
forms.ja: この町は小さい{わりに}、おいしい店がたくさんあります。
forms.en: This town has lots of good places to eat for its size.

forms.tag: その場合にしては · for (this one case)
forms.ja: 雨の日{にしては}、今日はお[客|きゃく]さんが多いですね。
forms.en: We have a lot of customers today, for a rainy day.

forms.ja: [彼|かれ]は自分で言い出した{くせに}、一[番|ばん]に帰ってしまいました。
forms.en: It was his idea, yet he was the first to go home.

check.label: Which one joins a noun directly?
check.q: [彼|かれ]は^[新人|しんじん]^（　　）、お[客|きゃく]さんとの話し方がとても上手です。
why: After a noun, わりに needs の: [新人|しんじん]のわりに. [新人|しんじん]わりに is not a form.
After a noun, くせに needs の too, and it blames. Here the new employee is being praised.
A noun joins にしては directly: for someone so new, he talks to customers very well.

drill.label: Choose the form
drill.q: ^たとえ^字が（　　）、手書きの手紙のほうが気持ちが[伝|つた]わります。
why: のに joins two real facts. たとえ imagines a case, so it needs ても or でも, not のに.
わりに measures a real fact against what you would expect. It does not go with たとえ.
下手 is a な-adjective, so たとえ…でも: even if your handwriting is poor, a handwritten letter carries your feelings better.
くせに blames a person for a real fact, and it does not go with たとえ. Nobody is being blamed here either.

drill.label: Choose the form
drill.q: 毎日料理をしている（　　）、^野菜を切ってスープにするぐらい^です。
why: [反面|はんめん] adds another side of the same thing. Here the second half only says what the cooking is, not another side of it.
The speaker does cook every day, but it is only chopping vegetables into a soup: といっても plays down what was just said, and 〜ぐらいです shows it is less than it sounds.
くせに blames someone. The speaker is describing their own cooking and is not criticising anyone.
にしては judges how something turned out against what you would expect, as in [初|はじ]めてにしては上手. 〜ぐらいです here only says what the cooking is, not how well it turned out.

drill.label: Build the sentence
tiles: 起こしても起こしても
drill.hint: Which tile says what happens however often I try to wake him? くせに follows the plain form, and the other days come after it.
drill.full: 弟は、学校がある日は{起こしても起こしても}起きない{くせに}休みの日は自分で早く起きます。
drill.explain: 起こしても起こしても, 起きない, くせに, 休みの日は. However many times I try to wake him, he does not get up: ても〜ても, then the plain form 起きない before くせに. くせに blames him, and 休みの日は sets his days off against school days: then he gets up early by himself.

drill.label: Choose the form
drill.q: このシャンプーは少し高い（　　）、^ぜひ一度試してみてください^。
why: [反面|はんめん] is followed by the other side of the same thing, told as a fact. A request like 試してみてください cannot follow it.
わりに is followed by how something turned out compared with what you would expect. A request cannot follow it.
のに cannot be followed by a request or an invitation.
けれど can lead into a request: it is a little expensive, but please try it once.

drill.label: Choose the form
drill.q: このかばんは^大きさ^の（　　）、とても軽いです。
why: A bag this big would be expected to be heavy, but this one is light: noun + の + わりに.
くせに blames a person. Here a bag is being praised.
にしては joins a noun directly, with no の, so 大きさのにしては is not a form.
ながらも also joins a noun directly (子どもながら), so 大きさのながらも is not a form.

drill.label: Build the sentence
drill.after: いないのがさびしいです。
drill.hint: [反面|はんめん] follows a な-adjective with な. Who is missing when you want to talk?
drill.full: 一人で住むのは気楽な{[反面|はんめん]}話したくても[相手|あいて]がいないのがさびしいです。
drill.explain: 気楽な, [反面|はんめん], 話したくても, [相手|あいて]が. [反面|はんめん] follows 気楽な and turns to the other side of living alone. 話したくても means even when I want to talk, and [相手|あいて]が goes with いない: there is no one to talk to.

exam.label: Choose the form
exam.q: 軽い気持ちで言った（　　）、あの一言はよくなかったと思う。
exam.explain: にしても accepts something and then gives the speaker's own judgement: even if it was said lightly, that remark was wrong. 反面 needs a second side of the same thing. わりに needs a result that is more or less than you would expect. くせに blames a person for what that same person does, but the second half here is the speaker's view of the remark.

exam.label: Choose the form
exam.q: 彼は先週の会議を休んだ（　　）、会議で決まったことにもんくを言っている。
exam.explain: He missed the meeting himself, yet he complains about what was decided there: くせに blames the same person for what he does. にしても needs the speaker's own judgement after it, not a report of what someone is doing. 反面 shows two sides of one thing, and ながらも does not follow the た form (休んだながらも is not a form).

exam.label: Build the sentence
exam.full: その選手はけがを{し}ながらも最後まで走りきった。
exam.explain: けがを, し, ながらも, 最後まで. ながらも joins the ます stem, so けがをする becomes けがをし before it. 最後まで goes with 走りきった: although he was injured, he ran all the way to the end.

scene.ja: アルバイトの求人広告
scene.intro: A café has put this job advertisement in its window. Tap each word on it.

check.label: How the exam asks it
check.q: 交通費は全額_支給_します。
check.explain: 支給 is read しきゅう: the shop pays all your travel costs. 支 is シ (as in 支店) and 給 is キュウ (as in 時給). しっきゅう adds a small っ, ちきゅう is a different word (the earth), and しきょう misreads 給.

skill.ask: Which charges apply to Yamada, and which of them are halved?
skill.passage:
みなみ市民センター　部屋の使い方
料金（1回）　和室1,000円／会議室1,500円／料理室2,000円
①市内に住んでいる方、または^市内の会社や学校に通っている方^は、^部屋の料金が半分になります^。
②会議室では、ピアノも使えます。^ピアノを使う場合は、部屋の料金のほかに500円かかります^。^ピアノの料金は半分になりません^。
③料理室を使う場合は、使う日の三日前までに申し込んでください。
④申し込みは、使う日の前の月の1日から受け付けます。
⑤部屋の中で食べ物を食べることはできません。ただし、料理室ではかまいません。
skill.strategy: First check whether Yamada can get the half price at all, then look for any charge that is not halved.

item.q: 山田さんは、となりの市に住んでいて、市内の会社で働いています。来月、会社の友だちと会議室を借りて、ピアノを使って歌の練習をします。山田さんたちは、いくら払いますか。
item.explain: Yamada lives in the next city but works at a company in this one, so rule ① applies: the meeting room costs half of 1,500円, which is 750円. The piano adds 500円 and is not halved (rule ②): 750 + 500 = 1,250円.
why: This is only the room at half price. Using the piano costs 500円 more (rule ②).
This halves the piano too, but rule ② says the piano charge is not halved.
This is the full price with no discount. Yamada works at a company in the city, so rule ① halves the room.
